text:
Based on the netlist and the spec table, my best guess is the Miller compensation capacitor `Cc`. I couldn't confirm this by simulation, so treat it as a ranked hypothesis.

The filter core is a unity-gain Sallen-Key low-pass (R1, R2, C2 to ground, C1 feedback), and its ideal values give fc near 279 MHz with Q around 0.23. That should show almost no peaking. The measured 126 MHz and 14.6 dB peaking therefore point to the op-amp's dynamics. Cc, Rz, and C1 are the elements that most directly control that, so they top the ranking. Power and DC level look consistent with the bias network, so I ruled those out.

```json
{"ranking": ["Cc", "Rz", "C1"], "fault": "Cc (Miller compensation cap, 1.428e-13 F) is wrong, likely resized from its designed value; this lowers op-amp GBW or phase margin in the unity-gain buffer, reducing fc and causing the excessive passband peaking"}
```
